mainTopic: Food and fires before שבת: מאכל בן דרוסאי, bread, the קרבן פסח, the בית המוקד fire, and how much of a fire must catch
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about fires before שבת and then explains it clause by clause. First, the גמרא sets the minimum cooking needed before שבת as מאכל בן דרוסאי, and shows the same measure used for בישולי גוים and for leaving food on an uncovered כירה. It then settles that the 'bottom' of the bread that must form a crust is the side stuck to the oven wall. The קרבן פסח may be lowered into the oven at nightfall because the חבורה is careful, since a whole פסח roasts slowly, unlike cut-up goat meat. The fire of the בית המוקד may be lit before שבת, and רב חסדא shows that this is because the כהנים are careful, not because of the פסוק 'בכל מושבותיכם'. Outside the מקדש, רב and שמואל argue over what 'most' of a bonfire means. For a single log, רב פפא requires most of both its thickness and its circumference. After a short side discussion of the word אח in ירמיהו, רב הונא and רב חסדא argue over whether bundled reeds and seeds need more burning or less, and a supporting statement begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Bonfires outside the מקדש need most of the wood burning
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends: in the גבולין, a bonfire may be lit before שבת only if the fire catches most of it while it is still day. רבי יהודה says that with coals, any amount is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the outlying areas, a bonfire may be lit only if there is enough time for the fire to catch most of it. רבי יהודה says: with coals, any amount is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the משנה. It contrasts the bonfire in the מקדש, which was allowed, with bonfires everywhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that a person will stir or fix a weak fire on שבת. If most of the fire has already caught before שבת, there is no reason to tend it. רבי יהודה holds that coals, once lit, stay lit, so even a small catch is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The outlying areas, meaning everywhere outside the מקדש

phrases.english: And in the outlying areas,
phrases.notes: In contrast to the bonfire in the בית המוקד in the מקדש, mentioned just before this.

phrases.english: only if there is time for the fire to take hold in most of it.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
With coals, any amount is enough.
phrases.notes: Coals do not go out once lit, so there is no worry that he will tend them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside the מקדש, a bonfire before שבת must have caught most of its wood. רבי יהודה says coals need only catch slightly.

steps.title: How much roasting is needed before שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking how much the food must be roasted before שבת starts.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its first question. It goes back to the earlier line in the משנה: meat may be roasted only if it can be roasted while it is still day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the food must be 'roasted while it is still day' but did not say how roasted. The גמרא wants the exact minimum. This step only asks the question; the answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This question is NOT about the bonfire you just read. It goes back to the earlier clause in the משנה about roasting meat before שבת.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And how much (must it be roasted)?
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's rule about roasting meat before שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא and returns to an earlier clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of cooking needed before שבת so that the food may finish cooking on שבת.

steps.title: The measure is מאכל בן דרוסאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רב, answers: the food must be roasted while it is still day to the level of מאכל בן דרוסאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רב: enough that they are roasted while it is still day like the food of בן דרוסאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question 'how much?' by giving a set measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן דרוסאי was a robber on the run. He ate his food only partly cooked, commonly explained as about one third done (some say half). Once food reaches that point it counts as edible, so there is less worry that he will stir the coals on שבת to hurry it along.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day, before שבת begins
Partly cooked food, like that eaten by the robber בן דרוסאי

steps.whyThisMatters: מאכל בן דרוסאי becomes a standard measure across many areas of halacha, as the next two steps show.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rav said:
Enough that they be roasted while it is still day
like the food of Ben Drosai.
phrases.notes: A robber who could not wait for his food to fully cook.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The food must reach the level of מאכל בן דרוסאי before שבת.

steps.title: The same measure removes the problem of food cooked by non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also uses the בן דרוסאי measure: food already cooked that much by a Jew has no problem of בישולי גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: anything that is already like the food of בן דרוסאי has no problem of בישולי גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא who uses the same measure of בן דרוסאי, this time in a different area of halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a Jew cooked the food up to the בן דרוסאי level and a non-Jew finished it, the food is still allowed. At that point it already counts as cooked food, so the non-Jew's work does not make it בישולי גוים. This shows that בן דרוסאי is a general measure for 'edible, counts as cooked'.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated, introducing a supporting statement from another אמורא
Food cooked by non-Jews, which the חכמים forbade

phrases.english: It was also stated:
phrases.notes: Here's another teaching that uses the same measure.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Anything that is like the food of Ben Drosai,
phrases.notes: Meaning it was already cooked to that point by a Jew.

phrases.english: has no problem of food cooked by gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 by showing the same measure used elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food cooked by a Jew to the level of מאכל בן דרוסאי is not affected by בישולי גוים.

steps.title: מאכל בן דרוסאי may stay on an unprepared כירה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes חנניא: food already at the בן דרוסאי level may be left on a כירה on שבת, even if the coals were not removed or covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: חנניא says: anything that is like the food of בן דרוסאי may be left on a stove, even if the stove is not swept or covered with ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same measure for the laws of leaving food on the fire on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, food may be left on a כירה only if the coals were swept out (גרופה) or covered with ash (קטומה), so he will not stir them. חנניא says that once food reaches the בן דרוסאי level, this is not needed. The food is already edible, so he has no reason to stir the coals.

keyTerms.meaning: To leave it on the fire

steps.whatToRemember: מאכל בן דרוסאי shows up in three places: the minimum roasting before שבת, removing בישולי גוים, and leaving food on an uncovered כירה (according to חנניא).
steps.whyThisMatters: חנניא's view is a key source in the halachic discussion of שהייה, leaving food on the fire on שבת.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Ḥananya says:
Anything that is like the food of Ben Drosai,
it is permitted to leave it on top of a stove

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין גְּרוּפָה וּקְטוּמָה.
phrases.english: even though it is not swept or covered with ashes.
phrases.notes: There is no worry that he will stir the coals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further source using the בן דרוסאי measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food at the בן דרוסאי level may be left on a כירה that is not גרופה וקטומה.

steps.title: Which bottom of the bread must form a crust?
steps.stepSummary: Turning to the bread in the משנה, the גמרא asks: when רבי אליעזר says the 'bottom' must form a crust, does he mean the side facing the oven wall or the side facing the fire?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may not place bread': They asked: is the 'bottom' the side toward the oven, or perhaps the side toward the fire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks what a word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the old style of oven, the dough was stuck to the inner wall, with the fire burning below. In the משנה, רבי אליעזר said the 'bottom' of the bread must form a crust before שבת. It is unclear which side counts as the 'bottom': the side pressed against the wall, or the side facing the fire.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them, a real unknown

phrases.english: 'One may not place bread' etc.:
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Is the 'bottom' the side that is next to the oven,
phrases.notes: The side stuck to the oven wall.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא תַּחְתּוֹן הַאיְךְ דְּגַבֵּי הָאוּר?
phrases.english: or perhaps the 'bottom' is the side that faces the fire?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the bread רבי אליעזר meant by 'bottom'.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the side stuck to the oven
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר directly: the side stuck to the oven must form a crust. That answers the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says: enough time that its surface stuck to the oven forms a crust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר says exactly which side he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states plainly that the side stuck to the oven wall must form a crust. So 'bottom' in the משנה means the side touching the oven, not the side facing the fire.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Enough time that its surface that is stuck to the oven forms a crust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'bottom' is the side stuck to the oven wall.

steps.title: Why may the קרבן פסח be lowered into the oven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the קרבן פסח may be lowered into the oven at nightfall, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may lower the פסח': What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks why it is allowed. This step sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other foods need to be partly cooked before שבת. Here, raw meat goes into the oven right at nightfall, so the גמרא wants to know why that is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח, the Paschal lamb

phrases.english: 'One may lower the Paschal lamb' (into the oven at nightfall):
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסח may go into the oven raw at nightfall.

steps.title: The group is careful
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the members of the חבורה eating the פסח are careful people and will not stir the coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the members of the group are careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason the משנה allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual worry is that someone will stir the coals on שבת. A group gathered to do a מצוה is careful, and they will remind each other, so the חכמים did not worry here.

keyTerms.meaning: The group registered together for one קרבן פסח
Careful, eager to do things properly

phrases.english: Because the members of the group are vigilant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חבורה is careful and will not stir the coals.

steps.title: But goat meat is allowed anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: does that mean it would otherwise be forbidden? But we learned that goat meat may go into the oven at nightfall whether the oven is sealed or not!
steps.simpleTranslation: But if not for that, it would not be allowed? Didn't the Master say: goat meat, whether the oven is sealed or not, is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason just given. It suggests there is no need for 'they are careful', because goat meat is already allowed for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A known teaching says goat meat may be put in the oven at nightfall even in an unsealed oven, because opening the oven to stir the coals would ruin the meat. A קרבן פסח is a lamb or goat, so the same rule should apply. Then why does the משנה need the special reason about the careful חבורה?

keyTerms.meaning: Does that mean that if not for this...
But didn't the Master say? Introduces a contradicting source
Sealed, with the oven closed with plaster

phrases.english: But if that were not so, it would not (be allowed)?!
But didn't the Master say:

phrases.aramaic: גַּדְיָא בֵּין שְׁרִיק בֵּין לָא שְׁרִיק —
phrases.english: A kid, whether (the oven) is sealed or not sealed,
it is fine!
phrases.notes: Opening the oven would harm the meat, so there is no worry that he will stir the coals.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָאו הָכִי לָא? וְהָאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the חבורה is careful.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Goat meat is allowed in any oven at nightfall, so the special reason should be unnecessary.

steps.title: There it was cut up; the פסח is whole
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the goat that is allowed everywhere was cut into pieces, while the פסח is roasted whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it was cut up; here it is not cut up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cut-up meat roasts quickly, so there is no reason to stir the coals. A whole פסח roasts slowly, so there really is a worry that he will stir the coals. That is why the משנה needs the reason that the חבורה is careful.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסח may go into the oven at nightfall only because the חבורה is careful. The general rule for goat meat applies only to meat cut into pieces, and the פסח is roasted whole.

phrases.english: There, it was cut into pieces;
here, it is not cut into pieces.
phrases.notes: The פסח must be roasted whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Goat meat is always allowed, so the careful-חבורה reason seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only cut-up goat meat is allowed generally. A whole פסח roasts slowly, so the reason that the חבורה is careful is needed.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the fire of the בית המוקד may be lit right before שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the fire of the בית המוקד may be lit close to nightfall and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may light the fire,' etc. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about lighting the fire in the בית המוקד, and asks for its source. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed lighting the big fire in the בית המוקד on ערב שבת, even though it will keep spreading after שבת starts. The גמרא wants to know what Torah source makes this allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: We light the fire (and let it catch)
From where are these things learned?
The Chamber of the Hearth in the מקדש, where the כהנים warmed themselves

phrases.english: And one may light the fire, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that allows lighting the בית המוקד fire before nightfall on ערב שבת

steps.title: רב הונא: 'in your dwellings' excludes the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא learns from 'לא תבערו אש בכל מושבותיכם' that the ban on lighting applies only in your homes, not in the בית המוקד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: 'Do not light fire in all your dwellings.' In your dwellings you may not light, but you may light in the fire of the בית המוקד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers with a פסוק. He reads the words 'your dwellings' as limiting the איסור to ordinary homes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in all your dwellings' seem extra, so רב הונא reads them as a limit. The מקדש is not 'your dwelling,' so lighting there is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
"You shall kindle no fire in all your dwellings"
phrases.notes: שמות לה:ג

phrases.english: In all your dwellings you may not kindle,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה מַבְעִיר בִּמְדוּרַת בֵּית הַמּוֹקֵד.
phrases.english: but you may kindle in the bonfire of the Chamber of the Hearth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק limits the ban to 'your dwellings,' so the מקדש fire is allowed

steps.title: רב חסדא: then it should be allowed even on שבת itself
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects that if the פסוק allows lighting in the מקדש, the fire could be lit on שבת itself, not just before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא challenged: If so, then even on שבת itself it should be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks רב הונא's source. It proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only allows lighting before שבת. But רב הונא's reading would allow lighting the בית המוקד fire on שבת itself. So his פסוק cannot be the real reason for the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda objected to it:
If so, even on Shabbat itself too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's derivation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The derivation would permit lighting on שבת itself, yet the משנה only allows it before שבת

steps.title: רב חסדא: the פסוק is about אברים and פדרים, and the כהנים are careful
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the פסוק allows burning קרבן parts on שבת. The בית המוקד fire may be lit before שבת only because כהנים are careful and will not stir the coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: When the פסוק came to permit something, it came to permit the limbs and fats of קרבנות. And the כהנים are careful people.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new explanation. The פסוק has nothing to do with the warming fire. The real reason is that כהנים are careful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's leniency is for real עבודה, burning אברים and פדרים on the מזבח. The warming fire of the בית המוקד is not עבודה. It may be lit before שבת only because there is no fear that careful כהנים will stoke it on שבת. This matches the reason given earlier for the פסח (Step 9).

keyTerms.meaning: The limbs and fats of קרבנות burned on the מזבח
The כהנים are careful and alert people

steps.whatToRemember: The בית המוקד fire is allowed before שבת because the כהנים are careful, not because of the פסוק. The פסוק only allows burning קרבן parts on שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
When the verse came to permit,
it came for limbs and fats,
and the priests are careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב הונא's derivation after the challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק and giving a new reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק permits the בית המוקד fire
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק permits burning קרבן parts on שבת. The warming fire is allowed before שבת because כהנים are careful.

steps.title: What does 'most of it' mean outside the מקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that outside the מקדש the fire must catch 'most of it' before שבת and asks what 'most' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And outside the מקדש, enough time for the fire to catch,' etc. What does 'most of them' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and asks for a definition. It is setting up the dispute that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the מקדש there is no assumption that people are careful. So the fire must already be well lit before שבת, so nobody will stir it. The question is how to measure 'most.'

phrases.english: And in the outlying areas, enough for it to catch, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: What is 'most of them'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The measure of 'most' for a fire outside the מקדש

steps.title: רב: most of every single log
steps.stepSummary: רב says each piece of wood must be mostly burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Most of each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the strict answer. Every log must be mostly on fire before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, it is not enough that the fire as a whole is going. Each log must have caught for most of its size.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of each and every one

phrases.english: Rav said:
Most of each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each log must be mostly burning

steps.title: שמואל: enough that no one needs to add kindling
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says it is enough if the fire burns well enough that no one would say 'bring thin wood to put underneath.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Enough so that people will not say, 'Bring wood and let us put it underneath them.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a more lenient measure. The fire only needs to be strong enough to keep going by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that someone will fix the fire on שבת. So שמואל measures by that concern: once the fire does not need help, it is fine. Every log does not need to be mostly burnt.

keyTerms.meaning: And we will place it beneath them

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Enough so that they will not say,
"Bring wood and we will place it beneath them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fire must be self-sustaining so no one needs to add kindling

steps.title: רב חייא's teaching supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא teaches a ברייתא (about lighting the מנורה) that a flame must rise by itself, which supports שמואל's measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא taught a ברייתא to support שמואל: So that the flame rises by itself, and not that the flame rises because of something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא defines a proper lighting as a flame that keeps going on its own. That is just what שמואל said: the test is whether the fire needs outside help.

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya taught to support Shmuel:
So that the flame will rise on its own,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שֶׁתְּהֵא שַׁלְהֶבֶת עוֹלָה עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר.
phrases.english: and not that the flame will rise because of something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's view
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a self-sustaining fire is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רב חייא

steps.title: A single log: thickness or circumference?
steps.stepSummary: For a single log, רב requires most of its thickness to catch. Another version of רב says most of its circumference.
steps.simpleTranslation: A single log: רב said most of its thickness. And some say: most of its circumference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from a bonfire to one log. It gives two versions of what רב said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one log there is no 'most of the logs,' so we need a measure inside the log itself. One version says the fire must go mostly deep (thickness). The other says it must go mostly around (circumference).

phrases.english: A single log:
Rav said: most of its thickness;
and some say: most of its circumference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the measure discussion to a single log
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two versions of רב: most of the thickness, or most of the circumference

steps.title: רב פפא: we need both
steps.stepSummary: Since we are unsure which version of רב is correct, רב פפא rules that both thickness and circumference must mostly catch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, we need most of its thickness and we need most of its circumference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the doubt by being strict both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know which version is really רב's. So we follow both, and the log must be mostly burnt in depth and around. That way we follow רב no matter which version is true.
steps.whatToRemember: For a single log before שבת, we need most of the thickness AND most of the circumference to catch.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Therefore we require most of its thickness
and we require most of its circumference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the doubt between the two versions

steps.title: The same dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two measures match a dispute of תנאים. רבי חייא says the wood must be ruined for a craftsman's use. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says the fire must catch from both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים. רבי חייא said: Enough that the wood is ruined for a craftsman's work. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: Enough that the fire catches from both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two measures for a single log already appear as a dispute among תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא gives a different test for when wood counts as 'burning.' One test is that the wood is useless to a craftsman. The other is that fire has caught on two sides. These two tests line up with the two versions of רב's measure.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of Tannaim:
Rabbi Chiyya said:
enough that the wood is ruined for a craftsman's work;
Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
enough that the fire catches from both sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the אמוראים' measures to a dispute of תנאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two tests for burning wood: ruined for a craftsman, or caught from both sides

steps.title: A hint from יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא adds that, even though it is not a true proof, a פסוק in יחזקאל hints to his view: wood burnt at both ends is no good for work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though there is no proof for this, there is a hint to it: 'The fire consumed both its ends, and its middle is charred. Is it fit for any work?'
steps.whatsHappening: A פסוק is brought as a hint, not a full proof, for the 'both sides' measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes wood burnt at both ends and asks whether it is still useful. This connects 'both sides' with 'useless for work.' Since it is only a זכר, it supports the idea without proving it.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no proof for the matter
A hint or allusion to the matter

steps.confusionAlert: A זכר לדבר is only a hint, not a real proof. Do not treat the פסוק as the actual source of the הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter:
"The fire consumed both of its ends,
and its middle is charred;
is it fit for work?"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל טו:ד

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a hint for רבי יהודה בן בתירא's measure
steps.raayaObject: Fire on both sides means the wood counts as burnt

steps.title: What is the אח in ירמיהו?
steps.stepSummary: Staying on the topic of fires, the גמרא quotes 'והאח לפניו מבוערת' and asks what אח means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the אח was burning before him.' What is אח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק about a burning fire and asks what one word means. It is setting up a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אח in the פסוק about יהויקים is unclear. The גמרא asks for its meaning because it connects to the topic of lighting wood.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in ירמיהו, usually translated 'hearth'

phrases.english: "And the ach was burning before him."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו לו:כב

phrases.english: What is ach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related tangent about burning wood
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word אח

steps.title: רב: willow; שמואל: wood lit 'in brotherhood'
steps.stepSummary: רב says אח is אחוונא, a willow. שמואל says it means wood lit with אחוונא, meaning pieces lit one from another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: אחוונא. And שמואל said: Wood that was lit with אחוונא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל explain the word אח in two ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, אחוונא is a kind of wood, willow. For שמואל, it comes from אחוה (brotherhood): pieces of wood that light each other. So it describes how the fire was lit.

keyTerms.meaning: Willow (per רב); or 'brotherhood,' wood lighting wood (per שמואל)

phrases.english: Rav said: willow (achvana).
And Shmuel said:
Wood that was lit with achvana (one from another).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the meaning of אח
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: willow. שמואל: wood lit piece from piece.

steps.title: A seller reveals that אחוונא means willow
steps.stepSummary: Someone in the market called out 'Who wants אחוונא?' and he turned out to be selling willow. This shows the word's meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to people: 'Who wants אחוונא?' It turned out to be willow.
steps.whatsHappening: A short story shows what the word אחוונא means in everyday speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People had forgotten what אחוונא meant. A seller used the word for willow, which confirms that אחוונא means willow. This fits רב's explanation.

phrases.english: A certain man who said to them:
"Who wants achvana?"
It turned out to be willow.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא דְּאָמַר לְהוּ מַאן בָּעֵי אַחְווֹנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the meaning of אחוונא

steps.title: Loose reeds and seeds need less burning than bundled ones
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that loose reeds and loose date seeds do not need most of the fuel burning before שבת. Bundled reeds, or seeds placed in baskets, do need most of the fuel burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Reeds do not need most of them to catch fire. If he tied them in a bundle, they need most to catch fire. Date seeds do not need most of them to catch fire. If he put them in baskets, they need most to catch fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic of a fire lit before שבת. רב הונא gives a new rule for two kinds of fuel, reeds and date seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that wood must catch to a certain degree before שבת so that no one will come to stir the fire on שבת. רב הונא says loose reeds and loose seeds catch fire easily, so they do not need most of the fuel burning. Once they are bundled or packed together, they act like a thick log, so most of the fuel must be burning.

keyTerms.meaning: He tied them together into a bundle
Date pits or seeds, used as fuel
Woven baskets, made of palm leaves

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear argument about whether packing fuel together makes it burn better or worse.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Reeds do not need most of them to catch fire,
phrases.notes: Loose reeds catch fire easily.

phrases.english: if he tied them in a bundle, they need most of them to catch fire.
phrases.notes: A bundle acts like a thick log.

phrases.english: Date seeds do not need most of them to catch fire,
if he placed them in baskets, they need most of them to catch fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion about the word אח to the rules for lighting a fire before שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loose reeds and seeds do not need most of the fuel burning. Bundled reeds and seeds in baskets do.

steps.title: Bundled fuel should burn better, not worse
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges רב הונא and says the opposite is more logical. Loose reeds and seeds scatter, while bundled ones stay together and burn well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: On the contrary, the reverse makes more sense! Loose reeds scatter, but bundled reeds do not scatter. Loose seeds scatter, but seeds placed in baskets do not scatter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks רב הונא's rule head-on. He argues that it should be completely flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא assumed that bundling makes fuel act like a log that is hard to light. רב חסדא says that loose fuel falls apart and spreads out, so the fire does not hold well. Bundled fuel stays together and keeps burning. So the loose fuel is the kind that should need most of it burning, not the bundled fuel.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying that bundling makes no difference. He accepts that there is a difference, but he flips which side needs most of the fuel burning.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda strongly objected to it:
On the contrary, the opposite makes sense:
loose reeds scatter,
if he bundled them, they do not scatter.
Loose seeds scatter,
if he placed them in baskets, they do not scatter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: אַדְּרַבָּה, אִיפְּכָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the logic of רב הונא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that bundled reeds and seeds in baskets need most of the fuel burning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Loose fuel scatters and does not hold a flame, while bundled fuel stays together. So loose fuel should be the stricter case, not bundled fuel.

steps.title: Introducing a supporting statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with 'it was also stated' to bring another teaching that backs up one of the views. The statement itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote another teaching that agrees with one of the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי tells us that another אמורא taught the same idea on his own. That gives extra support to one side of the argument between רב הונא and רב חסדא. We find out which side on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated, introducing a teaching that agrees with an earlier view

phrases.english: It was also stated
phrases.notes: The supporting quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins bringing outside support for one side of the argument in steps 27 and 28.
steps.raayaObject: One of the two views about loose fuel versus bundled fuel
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching by another אמורא, quoted on the next amud
